title: The Opinion That Grew More Certain
title_ja: ますます確信された意見
fact_notes: 人物・出来事・制度は架空の思考実験。実在の調査・統計・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: Imagine a group of students discussing a proposal to replace printed school newsletters with a digital version that parents could read on their phones.
sentences.ja: 紙の学校便りを保護者が携帯で読める電子版に置き換える案を議論する生徒たちを想像しよう。

sentences.en: At the beginning of the conversation, most participants have only a tentative preference based on their own experiences with printed and electronic information.
sentences.ja: 会話の最初、多くの参加者は紙と電子情報の自分の経験に基づく暫定的な好みしか持たない。

sentences.en: One student argues enthusiastically that a digital version would be easier to distribute, and several others contribute examples that appear to support her position.
sentences.ja: 一人は電子版の方が配布しやすいと熱心に主張し、他の数人もそれを支持するように見える例を出す。

sentences.en: By the end of the meeting, the group seems much more certain about the proposal, although it has obtained little new information from people outside the discussion.
sentences.ja: 会議の終わりには外部の人々から新情報をほとんど得ていないのに、グループは案にずっと確信を持ったように見える。

sentences.en: A teacher who observed the conversation asks the students to distinguish between the amount of evidence supporting a conclusion and the number of times that evidence has been repeated in different words.
sentences.ja: 会話を観察した教師は結論を支える証拠量と同じ証拠が別の言葉で繰り返された回数を区別するよう求める。

sentences.en: Several students realize that they have described essentially the same advantage of electronic distribution rather than presenting independent reasons that would address different aspects of the proposal.
sentences.ja: 数人は案の異なる側面に対処する独立した理由でなく、電子配布の本質的に同じ利点を述べていたと気づく。

sentences.en: They also notice that a student who had raised concerns about families with limited access to digital devices stopped contributing after her first comment received little attention.
sentences.ja: 電子機器へのアクセスが限られた家庭について懸念を述べた生徒が最初の発言があまり注目されなかった後、発言しなくなったことにも気づく。

sentences.en: The apparent consensus may therefore reflect both the repetition of familiar arguments and the disappearance of concerns that were not actively investigated.
sentences.ja: そのため見かけの合意は身近な主張の反復と積極的に調査されなかった懸念の消失を反映しているかもしれない。

sentences.en: For a second discussion, the students agree to make a record of distinct reasons for and against the proposal before attempting to reach a collective judgment.
sentences.ja: 第二回議論では集団的判断を下す前に案の賛否それぞれの異なる理由を記録することにする。

sentences.en: Each reason is accompanied by a description of the evidence that would help determine whether the underlying assumption is appropriate for the particular school.
sentences.ja: 各理由に、その学校で背後の前提が適切か判断するために役立つ根拠の説明を添える。

sentences.en: The teacher encourages participants to identify what kind of information might lead them to reconsider their own position rather than merely searching for further examples that confirm it.
sentences.ja: 教師は現在の立場を確認する追加例だけを探すのでなく、それを見直すきっかけとなる情報の種類を特定するよう促す。

sentences.en: They discover that the strongest objection to one version of the plan might be addressed by modifying its design rather than by rejecting electronic distribution entirely.
sentences.ja: 計画の一形態に対する最も強い反論は電子配布を全面拒否せず設計を修正して対処できるかもしれないと分かる。

sentences.en: The class decides that seeking further information about family preferences and access would be more appropriate than immediately declaring that either format is superior in every respect.
sentences.ja: どちらかが全点で優れるとすぐ宣言するより家庭の好みやアクセスについて情報を求める方が適切だと判断する。

sentences.en: Students acknowledge that the original conversation was not necessarily useless simply because their confidence increased more rapidly than the evidence available to them.
sentences.ja: 確信が根拠より急速に増えたからといって最初の会話が必ずしも無益だったわけではないと認める。

sentences.en: It helped identify potential benefits that could become the subject of a more systematic investigation if the students were prepared to consider information that challenged their expectations.
sentences.ja: それは期待に反する情報も考慮する用意があればより体系的調査の対象になる潜在的利点を特定する助けとなった。

sentences.en: Their revised process therefore preserves the opportunity to develop ideas through conversation while creating a separate stage in which those ideas are examined critically.
sentences.ja: 修正手順は会話によって考えを発展させる機会を残しつつ、考えを批判的に吟味する別段階を作る。

sentences.en: The thought experiment illustrates a difference between becoming more convinced of a conclusion and acquiring stronger reasons for believing that the conclusion is correct.
sentences.ja: この思考実験は結論にますます確信を持つことと結論が正しいと信じるより強い理由を得ることの違いを示す。

sentences.en: Repeated agreement can make a position feel increasingly familiar without necessarily increasing the amount or independence of the evidence supporting it.
sentences.ja: 賛同の繰り返しはそれを支える根拠の量や独立性を必ずしも高めず立場を身近に感じさせ得る。

sentences.en: A productive discussion should therefore make room for questions about what remains unknown as well as arguments about which available option currently seems most attractive.
sentences.ja: 有益な議論は現在どの案が最も魅力的かについての主張に加え、何がまだ分からないかの問いも許容すべきだ。

sentences.en: The quality of a collective judgment depends not merely on the strength with which it is expressed but on the relationship between its degree of certainty and the evidence from which it is drawn.
sentences.ja: 集団的判断の質は表明の強さだけでなく確信の程度とそこから導かれる根拠の関係に依存する。

options: Replacing printed newsletters with digital ones.

questions.prompt: What was unusual about the group's growing confidence?
options: The proposal had already been tested for years.
Little new outside evidence had been obtained.
All participants had changed their minds.

questions.prompt: What distinction did the teacher highlight?
options: Amount of evidence versus repetition of evidence.

questions.prompt: Why might apparent consensus be misleading?
options: Everyone had signed a formal agreement.
A concern lost attention and arguments were repeated.
questions.explanation_ja: 反論が検討されなかった。

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of identifying evidence that could change one's position?
options: Encourage testing assumptions rather than only confirming them.
questions.explanation_ja: 確認だけでなく見直す根拠。

options: The price of every device worldwide.
questions.explanation_ja: 家庭の希望とアクセス。

questions.prompt: Why preserve conversation in the revised process?
options: It can generate ideas that are then examined critically.
It eliminates the need for evidence.
questions.explanation_ja: 考えの生成と吟味を分ける。

questions.prompt: What does tentative mean in the passage?

options: Discussion should always end with a unanimous decision.
Confidence should be proportionate to the quality and independence of evidence.

grammar.focus: although it has obtained little new information
grammar.explanation_ja: althoughで確信と新情報を対比。

paraphrases.source: By the end of the meeting, the group seems much more certain about the proposal, although it has obtained little new information from people outside the discussion.
paraphrases.rewrite: The group became more confident despite receiving little outside evidence.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 根拠が乏しいまま確信が増えた。

paraphrases.source: Several students realize that they have described essentially the same advantage of electronic distribution rather than presenting independent reasons that would address different aspects of the proposal.
paraphrases.rewrite: They restated one benefit instead of presenting distinct reasons about different issues.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 同一の利点を繰り返した。

paraphrases.source: The teacher encourages participants to identify what kind of information might lead them to reconsider their own position rather than merely searching for further examples that confirm it.
paraphrases.rewrite: The teacher asked what evidence could make students revise their views.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 再考を促す根拠を考える。

paraphrases.source: The quality of a collective judgment depends not merely on the strength with which it is expressed but on the relationship between its degree of certainty and the evidence from which it is drawn.
paraphrases.rewrite: A group judgment should be evaluated by how its confidence relates to the evidence, not just how strongly it is expressed.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 表明の強さより根拠との関係。

discourse.role_ja: 確信増加と根拠の乏しさ。
